system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A subject/placed_subject/replacement_subject reference supplies its selected identity properties, not its original background, pose or photographic lighting. An environment reference supplies its scene, not the depicted actor identity or actor-specific appearance. An observed claim copying a mixed source summary must obey the same responsibility: citing the source does not authorize importing all its content. Independently requested or creative content is allowed; a generic car or room resembling a source is not itself evidence of misuse. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only references preserve their role-specific recipient and do not play the original recording; voice, new-score style, cut/action timing and new sound texture are distinct relationships, never general permission to condition any new sound. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.
The typed claims preserve their explicit origins. A user-origin claim records caller authorization or a requested outcome; it is not itself evidence that the final narrative executes that outcome or copies an original signal. User claims are deliberately absent from executable fragment addresses. Compare the actual final narrative, source bindings and typed performance events to that authorization. Observed and creative claims remain auditable executable assertions.
reference_sheet_identity_contract is host-selected: these explicit reference-sheet assets supply non-frame identity, not actual first/last-frame pixels. Audit the ACTUAL canonical target descriptor and attributes in subject definition fragments against the original source traits and caller claims. Accepted target identity has priority over source conflicts, but that does not authorize sheet labels, panel captions, camera/view/close-up packaging, sheet layout, source pose or background to become identity facts. A sheet caption is not a target name without independent caller authorization. A mixed stable physical trait plus view wording must retain the trait and remove only its view packaging; do not discard a genuine eye color, scar, horn, garment or other physical fact to make cleanup easier. The earlier qualification's existence is not proof of successful cleanup. Report source_presentation_in_identity for clear remaining presentation in actual canonical fields, citing the exact subject definition fragment and subject_id from this host-selected contract. Its quote must be exact actual descriptor, attribute or description text, not JSON field syntax, raw source attribution Details, evidence, retention metadata or an unrelated fragment. This concerns the IR identity sent to H3, not proof that text appears in a generated video. Do not report a caller-authorized name or genuine markings as a panel label merely because similar text occurs on the sheet. Sources used as actual frames are absent from this contract: their panels, captions and full composition remain target frame content and must be preserved. Do not remove them or report a whole-sheet animation as identity contamination.
The request has multiple identity-source candidates. Check subject_projections and the caller's complete request: one identifiable target may combine separately selected properties from several sources. Every requested source/property contribution must be present in that target's actual typed attributes and source attribution details, consistent with subject_projections and the quoted caller requirements. A descriptor or summary claiming a contribution does not replace a missing typed attribute or the wrong source/property selection. The subject definition fragments expose the complete ledger for exact finding quotes. Reject subject_projection_mismatch when a requested contribution is missing or assigned to the wrong source, or when the final actual narrative clearly duplicates that same requested target as separate actors, combines distinct requested actors contrary to the request, changes the selected target category (for example a car into an unspecified object), or imports source properties that its accepted projection excluded, including properties sneaked into its target descriptor. A new unrelated permitted actor is not automatically a duplicate. Cite the exact contradictory final fragment. Source resemblance alone is not identity authorization.

claims.text: The woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground in a cinematic Hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements.
Smoke, broken standards, scattered fires, embers, blackened stone, ash fall, and the burning plain are added to fill the battleground setting.
A restrained low orchestral score with dark brass and a slow percussive pulse is newly generated.

fragments.music: A restrained, low orchestral score with dark brass and a slow percussive pulse, newly generated; no source audio is reused.
fragments.shot:shot-1:description: Smoke rolls across a war-torn plain at dusk, broken standards leaning in churned earth and scattered fires glowing orange beneath a bruised sky. A low ridge of blackened stone and a toppled banner frame the edge of the field while ash falls like dirty snow. <Subject:subject-2> drives forward low and fast, charcoal-black scales flashing blue-gray, long pale horns swept back, dorsal spikes rising along its neck, membranous wings half-spread and spiked tail whipping behind. <Subject:subject-1> leans low over the dragon's neck, black technical jacket cinched with straps and buckles, dark crew-neck top and cargo trousers pressed flat by the wind, combat boots braced against the scales. The beast bursts through a curtain of smoke as embers streak past, and the pair surges from the haze into the open battleground.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: Smoke and distant fires establish the battleground as the dragon and rider enter the field.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:1: The dragon surges through smoke while the rider leans low over its neck.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:2: Deep rushing wind, leathery wingbeats, distant battle roar, and cracking fire.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:3: Embers streak past as the pair drives forward through the haze.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:4: The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: Firelight catches <Subject:subject-1>'s face as she rides, jaw set and eyes narrowed with fierce resolve, the small scar above one eyebrow highlighted by the glow. Her short dark hair with shaved sides and tied-back topknot whips against her cheek, and the jacket collar snaps in the wind. Firelight ripples across the buckles and zipper of the black technical jacket, while her weathered hands hold steady and her lean athletic build stays braced low. Behind her, <Subject:subject-2>'s pale horns and dorsal spikes cut across the frame while its wingbeat rocks the air and sends grit skittering across the scales. The burning battlefield slides past as a soft blur of orange and black beyond the dragon's shoulder.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: Firelight reveals the rider's face and the dragon's pale horns and dorsal spikes behind her.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:1: She rides with jaw set while her hair and jacket collar snap in the wind.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:2: A close percussive wingbeat thump and wind buffeting fabric and hair.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:3: Her narrowed eyes hold steady as the wingbeat rocks the air around her.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:4: The camera arcs around the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.shot:shot-3:description: A wide sweep of the burning plain opens around the pair. <Subject:subject-1> rises in the saddle as <Subject:subject-2> banks hard, membranous wings snapping wide across the sky and spiked tail trailing through the smoke. The dragon sweeps over the embattled ground, where broken formations, toppled standards, and distant fires spread beneath the shadow of its body. Charcoal-black scales catch the firelight, pale horns cutting a sharp silhouette against the smoke while the rider lifts one weathered hand to brace against the wind. Wing-wash flattens the grass and scatters loose ash below, and the burning plain opens out around them in a vast, churned panorama of smoke, embers, and ruined ground.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:0: The rider rises in the saddle as the dragon banks hard.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:1: Membranous wings snap wide over the burning plain while the spiked tail trails through smoke.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:2: A vast wing-wash of air, low battlefield rumble, and crackling flame.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:3: The dragon's silhouette cuts against the smoke above the embattled ground.
fragments.shot:shot-3:event:4: The camera pulls out with large amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.soundscape: Deep rushing wind over leathery wingbeats, close percussive wing thumps, distant rolling battle roar, crackling fire, and wing-wash over the plain, all newly generated.
